This musician recorded Cole Porter standards in the first album of her Song Book series, which inaugurated Norman Granz’s Verve Records. This “First Lady of Song” was known for her scat singing.
This Cole Porter song is the first track on the 1972 album Ella Loves Cole. To comply with the Hays Code, Porter edited a lyric from this song about cocaine to “Some like the perfume from Spain.”

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about people associated with interwar pan-Africanist organizations, like the International African Service Bureau in London, for 10 points each.
parts: The IASB’s organizing secretary Chris Brathwaite emigrated from this then-colony with the British merchant navy. Sandra Mason served as the first president of this Caribbean country when it became a republic in 2021.

The IASB’s newsletter Africa and the World was edited by the historian C. L. R. James, whose work The Black Jacobins analyzed the influence of French revolutionary ideals on this leader of the Haitian Revolution.

Three years before publishing The Black Jacobins, James wrote a play about Toussaint, who was played by this man at its London premiere. This man was the longtime chairman of the Council of African Affairs.

bonuses.leadin: This author started the journal The Contemporary as a financial venture that included Nikolai Gogol among its editors. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this poet, who had his literary ventures taken over after dying in a duel in a manner similar to Lensky from his poem Eugene Onegin.

This author had a scathing critique of the aristocracy removed from the end of the public version of his poem commemorating Pushkin’s death, “Death of the Poet.” This author also wrote A Hero of Our Time.

After The Contemporary was taken over by Nikolay Nekrasov, this critic joined to promote western liberal ideas. The ideological radicalization of The Contemporary continued under this man’s successor, Nikolay Chernychevsky.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the social psychologist Susan Fiske, for 10 points each.
parts: With Peter Glick and Amy Cuddy, Fiske modeled these biases along the dimensions of warmth and competence. These biases are generalized beliefs about particular groups of people.

Along with Glick, Fiske developed a 22-item inventory for this two-word framework, which claims that its central attitude is composed of benevolent and hostile subtypes, depending on their evaluations of gender.

Fiske coined the “cognitive miser” to describe how people minimize cognitive effort when problem-solving, based on these two thinkers’ paper “Judgment Under Uncertainty.” These two thinkers developed prospect theory.

bonuses.leadin: In his memoirs, Carl Czerny (“CHAIR-nee”) claimed that all Viennese pianists around 1800 were either “Beethovenists” or followers of this composer. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this composer who succeeded Haydn as the Esterházy family’s court composer. This composer’s best known piece is a trumpet concerto in E major.

Czerny and Hummel exemplify a late-Classical style named for this adjective that emphasized the virtuosity of composer-pianists. Chopin’s works in that style include a polonaise titled for this adjective and “grande,” which he paired with the Andante spianato.

Composers of the stile brillante (“STEEL bree-YAHNT”) favored this form consisting of a refrain separated by episodes. A movement in this form from Mozart’s Piano Sonata No. 11 imitates Turkish music.

bonuses.leadin: A colony that was established at the mouth of this river named a fort that was commanded by Lion Gardiner during its siege in 1636. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this river along which the Saybrook Colony developed. This was the longest river along which the Western Niantics and Mohegans fought in the Pequot War.
The first governor of the Saybrook Colony was from this family and later helped consolidate the Connecticut Colony. John Wheelwright split from a man from this family who was backed by Thomas Dudley.
Noblemen from this religious sect were granted a patent by Robert Rich to establish the Saybrook Colony. This religious group also established the Massachusetts Bay Colony.

bonuses.leadin: CASY technology is used to count these entities without the need for an electrolyte reservoir, unlike a similar apparatus invented by Walter Coulter. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these entities that are loaded into a Neubauer counting chamber etched with five different size grids. The viability of these entities can be determined by using propidium iodide or Trypan blue staining.

Metabolic cell viability assays often quantify the amount of this molecule produced, such as after adding a firefly luciferase. This molecule is mostly generated by a namesake synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Another common colorimetric viability assay uses this dye, known by a three-letter acronym, which is converted into the purple compound formazan by cellular oxidoreductases.

bonuses.leadin: Two pink-faced police officers hold batons in a painting by this artist that features the word DEFACEMENT followed by a question mark in the background. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this artist of The Death of Michael Stewart. A cage-like top hat sits on top of a black figure in this artist’s painting Irony of Negro Policeman.
Irony of Negro Policeman was painted shortly after Basquiat’s move away from this medium towards gallery art. Banksy is another artist who works in this medium.

Irony of Negro Policeman was painted the same year as this other Basquiat painting, one of the few works of white men painted by Basquiat. This painting depicts a menacing white police figure wearing a peaked cap.

bonuses.leadin: In The Tale of Genji, one of these animals named Okinamaro is temporarily exiled from the palace until the Emperor forgives it after it starts crying. For 10 points each:
parts: What animals also name a group of warriors that title a Kyokutei Bakin novel set during the Ashikaga period that is considered the longest novel in Japanese history?

The narrator falls in love with a girl who dies after contracting the plague from the village dog Leo in this author’s novel Nip the Buds, Shoot the Kids. This author also wrote the semi-autobiographical novel A Personal Matter.

A dog named after Charles Lindbergh is gifted to Hiroshi, the son of Kaname and Misako in this Jun’ichirō Tanizaki novel. Kaname gets drawn into his father-in-law’s obsession with Bunraku theater in this novel.

bonuses.leadin: In one tale, a fox, a squirrel, and a bear help this figure steal fire from the island of the fire spirits. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this trickster spirit from Anishinaabe folklore who created the thunderbird to fend off the underwater panther among other spirits. This Ojibwe trickster often takes the form of a hare.

The beardless depiction of this figure’s statue at Lake Bemidji (“buh-MIJ-ee”) is apparently attributed to Nanabozho’s walloping of this figure with a Red Lake walleye. Babe the Blue Ox was this lumberjack’s companion.
Among the various adversaries of Nanabozho are these emaciated spirits known to possess starving men like “Swift Runner” who are sometimes diagnosed with their namesake psychosis.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about methods used to quantify antibody–antigen binding affinities. For 10 points each:
parts: This word partially names an effect where plasmon resonances change intensity due to binding events. This word also names an “enhanced” form of Raman spectroscopy used to detect trace biomarkers on gold nanoparticles.

Direct thermodynamic data for binding can be obtained using the isothermal titration form of this technique, whose “bomb” type measures heat of reactions at constant volume and can be crudely done with Styrofoam cups.

A form of this technique measures antibody affinity by finding equilibrium concentrations of free ligands across a semi-permeable membrane. The Donnan type of this technique alternatively uses ion exchange membranes.
